en: Baguio City has a subtropical highland climate, making it much cooler than the rest of the Philippines due to its high elevation.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol are made of thousands of cone-shaped limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for having one of the most perfectly symmetrical volcanic cones in the world.
Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a giant, persistent storm that has been raging in the planet's atmosphere for over three hundred years.
Sirius, also known as the Dog Star, is the brightest star visible in the night sky from Earth.
The Apollo 11 astronauts landed in the Sea of Tranquility, a large, dark basaltic plain on the Moon's surface.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River collects rainfall from the mountains and flows underground for eight kilometers before emptying into the sea.
Laterite soil, often called brick earth, is rich in iron and aluminum and is commonly used to make building bricks in the Philippines.
Saturn is the only planet in our solar system with a density low enough that it could theoretically float in water.
The Marikina Valley Fault System is a major geological fracture in the Philippines capable of generating strong, damaging earthquakes.
Typhoon Yolanda, known internationally as Haiyan, was one of the strongest tropical cyclones ever recorded to make landfall.
Farmers carved the Banaue Rice Terraces directly into the steep metamorphic rock mountains of the Cordilleras over two thousand years ago.
